    Use strong contrast between oversized rounded masses and exceptionally narrow elongated structures.

    Simplify facial anatomy into memorable illustrated shapes while preserving defining features of recognizable people or characters.

C₃  EXPRESSIVE DRY-BRUSH TEXTURES + HAND-DRAWN CONSTRUCTION
    Render the entire character through a combination of opaque gouache-like color fills, scratchy colored-pencil strokes, dry-brush marks, broken ink lines, and irregular hand-painted texturing.
    FUR: Suggest shaggy, coarse, uneven fur using hundreds of loose directional pencil and dry-brush strokes, sparse protruding strands, scratchy tufts, and intentionally inconsistent density.     SKIN: Use simplified matte color shapes, sparse pencil hatching, subtle pigment variation, irregular spots, and occasional sketchy crease lines. No realistic skin shaders.
    CLOTHING: Reinterpret [SIGNATURE_OUTFIT] using broad irregular painted shapes, rough fabric outlines, loosely drawn seams, simplified knitted patterns, sweater ribs, stitched accents, and short dry-brush strokes that suggest worn fibers.
    HARD DETAILS: Render horns, teeth, claws, shoes, accessories, or structural parts with simplified flat shapes, rough painted edges, sparse crosshatching, and a few graphic highlights.
    Allow certain marks to extend slightly beyond painted boundaries. Keep contours imperfect and intentionally handmade.

C₄  MUTED GOUACHE PALETTE + ILLUSTRATED COLOR BEHAVIOR
    Use a restricted painterly palette based on muted slate blue, dusty blue-gray, faded lavender, warm cream, parchment beige, burnt orange, rusty terracotta, charcoal black, and subdued ochre.
    Adapt the actual color choices to [SUBJECT] while preserving the reference's quiet warm-cool harmony and restrained saturation.
    Apply colors in broad, mostly flat hand-painted regions with imperfect boundaries and occasional paper-grain exposure.
    Introduce sparse dark spots, isolated warm accents, irregular patches, loose scribbled highlights, and lightly textured overlapping pigment where relevant.
